nodes.summary: 02 · Long Document — Reads like a memo, a letter, or a journal entry. No marketing structure. Continuous prose with inline section heads. The page is *literature* about the product.

nodes.name: 03-marquee-hero.md
nodes.summary: 03 · Marquee Hero — The hero IS the page above the fold. A single bold statement or visual fills the viewport. No subhead, no CTA in fold. Below the fold the page becomes something else (a list, a grid, prose).

nodes.name: 04-stat-led.md
nodes.summary: 04 · Stat-Led — The hero is a giant number — a metric, a count, a percentage. Everything that follows supports or qualifies it. Data is the narrative.

nodes.name: 05-workbench.md
nodes.summary: 05 · Workbench — Product screenshots in frames are the primary content. The page is a guided tour of the app in use. Less marketing copy, more "here's what you do with it."

nodes.name: 06-conversational-faq.md
nodes.summary: 06 · Conversational FAQ — Bold questions, brief answers. The page reads like an honest interview with the product. Often each Q/A is a collapsible accordion.

nodes.name: 07-manifesto.md
nodes.summary: 07 · Manifesto — Polemical large type. Declaration energy. The page tells the reader what to believe before it tells them what to buy. Often political-poster aesthetic.

nodes.name: 08-photographic.md
nodes.summary: 08 · Photographic — A single huge image dominates each fold. Text is small annotation, not headline. The design says *look* before it says *read*.

nodes.name: 09-quote-led.md
nodes.summary: 09 · Quote-Led — The hero is a pull-quote with attribution. The headline is borrowed credibility, not the brand's voice. The page leads with social proof.

nodes.name: 10-specimen.md
nodes.summary: 10 · Specimen *(no longer the default)* — Numbered left-margin labels, huge serif display, asymmetric column spans, hairline rules, typographic-only CTA, generous whitespace. Editorial / type-foundry energy.

nodes.name: 11-catalogue.md
nodes.summary: 11 · Catalogue — Uniform grid of variations of the same thing — typefaces, colour palettes, product SKUs. The page is a visual index of inventory.

nodes.name: 12-letter.md
nodes.summary: 12 · Letter — First-person, written, intimate. Opens with a greeting ("Dear friend,"). No buttons in the fold. Reads as a personal note from the founder.

nodes.name: 13-index-first.md
nodes.summary: 13 · Index-First — The page IS a list of links. No hero image, no narrative flow. Pure navigation as design.

nodes.name: 14-narrative-workflow.md
nodes.summary: 14 · Narrative Workflow — Numbered stages tell the story of how the user uses the product over time. Each section is a phase (1.0 → 2.0 → 3.0 → 4.0). The page is a process timeline.

nodes.name: 15-split-studio.md
nodes.summary: 15 · Split Studio — Diptych. Every major content block divides the screen — text on one side, proof on the other. The pairing alternates direction down the page.

nodes.name: 16-feature-stack.md
nodes.summary: 16 · Feature Stack — Sticky left pane (label / description) + scroll-synced right pane (screenshots cycling through related details). Cinematic pacing.

nodes.name: 17-type-specimen.md
nodes.summary: 17 · Type Specimen — The typeface IS the design. Foundry homepage or design-system marketing where a custom typeface is the brand's proof.

nodes.name: 18-portfolio-grid.md
nodes.summary: 18 · Portfolio Grid — Filterable cards of projects. Studio or designer homepages where the work is the product.

nodes.name: 19-map-diagram.md
nodes.summary: 19 · Map / Diagram — A single large spatial diagram organises the page — flowchart, floor plan, network graph, system map. Information is laid out *spatially*, not linearly.

nodes.name: 20-ecosystem-index.md
nodes.summary: 20 · Ecosystem Index — Multiple discovery surfaces — featured / latest / by category / by people. The platform's value is emergence and browsing, not declaration.

nodes.name: 21-component-playground.md
